label: main season
summary: Recommend clearance for sign-off: E3 is weak indirect evidence—a second-hand, unlocated report—and remains unexplained after the area’s two non-technical survey visits. National criteria make such evidence a clearance target after two visits, and technical survey is unavailable. E1 and E2 do not establish safe use or absence of EO.
flags: E3 is hearsay and does not locate the reported event within the area; the recommendation follows the national follow-up threshold rather than direct confirmation.
The survey team could reach only the edge and did not see the land inside. The zone visit flag and survey priority are not evidence.

checks.detail: Every item of the evidence log is in the register.
The national criteria provide no technical survey, so clearance takes its place; evidence to target: E3.

E1.quote: The people at the community meeting had moved to the vereda in the last 2 years and could not say how the area was used before.
E1.note: The meeting participants lack knowledge of the area's earlier use, so their statement neither supports EO presence nor its absence.

E2.quote: The survey team could reach only the edge of the area, because rain had closed the trail into it, and could not see the land inside.
E2.note: This is a reliable account of limited access, but it reports no observation about EO presence or absence inside the area.

E3.quote: A shopkeeper in the village said neighbours told her that an animal was killed by a mine somewhere in the area some years ago.
E3.note: This is an unlocated second-hand report relayed by an informant whose underlying witnesses cannot be identified as first-hand sources; it suggests possible EO but does not confirm it.
